title: Typed Frame Handshake and Failover Playbook (PRD sketch)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working PRD sketch proposing a typed-frame streaming surface and client handshake that:
- makes partial/structured output predictable for SDKs,
- explicitly models tool-call handoffs inside a stream,
- defines graceful failure/fallback semantics (including offline resume tokens and degraded JSON-only fallbacks),
- provides a clear SDK contract for backpressure, interruption, and checkpointing.

Problem statement:
Teams building interactive features require consistent behavior when the model emits partial text, structured events (tables, JSON blobs), and instructions to call external tools. Today, clients fork logic across bespoke SDKs: ad-hoc frame parsing, inconsistent retries for tool calls, and opaque failure behavior when a stream aborts mid-toolcall. This leads to brittle integrations, duplicated server-side logic, and poor UX on flaky networks.

Goals (success criteria):
- API surface that allows clients to consume a single stream and react to typed frames rather than freeform text blobs.
- Deterministic semantics for tool_call lifecycle in-stream: start, progress, result, and abort.
- Built-in resume tokens / checkpoint frames so idempotent clients can recover without replaying entire context.
- SDK ergonomics: minimal callback surface, clear backpressure primitives, and typed response objects in JS/Python.
- Migration path: existing streaming endpoints supported; new behavior opt-in via header or versioned route.

Non-goals:
- Replacing all existing streaming protocols in one go.
- Designing a binary wire format (we’ll remain JSON-over-chunked-HTTP/HTTP2/WS).
- Solving all client-side UI concerns (we provide primitives, not UI components).

High-level design overview:
1) Frame model (explicit "frame_type" field on each chunk)
   - partial_text: incremental plain text pieces (relative offsets optional)
   - structured_event: typed JSON payload (schema name + payload)
   - tool_call_start: intent + tool metadata + request id
   - tool_call_progress: progress ping for long-running tool actions (status, percent)
   - tool_call_result: final result object (possibly binary reference or structured JSON)
   - checkpoint: opaque resume token that encodes minimal state (model version, cursor, tool-call id map)
   - error: structured error model (code, message, retryable boolean)
   - resume_hint: optional human-readable hint for client to resume gracefully

2) Handshake and versioning
   - Clients opt into typed frames via header: "Accept-Redwood-Frames: v1" or by using new endpoint /v1/responses/stream-frames.
   - Server replies with initial handshake frame: frame_type: "session_init" including server-supported features (tool_call_retries, max_checkpoint_interval_ms, recommended_chunk_size).

3) Tool calling lifecycle inside streams
   - When model decides to call a tool, server emits tool_call_start with a generated call_id. The client SDK exposes a promise-like object for the call.
   - If the client is configured to proxy the call to a backend, SDK exposes hook to map call_id -> handler. SDK also supports auto-proxy mode (call server-managed tool) vs. client-managed (local service handles it).
   - tool_call_progress frames update any long-running call state.
   - tool_call_result finalizes and ties back into model continuation frames. If the stream stops before tool_call_result, the checkpoint frame must contain enough mapping for resume.

4) Checkpoints, resume tokens, and idempotency
   - Checkpoints are emitted periodically (configurable by server and hinted in handshake). They are opaque strings but encode: model snapshot id, sequence cursor, and short hashed map of pending tool_call_ids.
   - Client can re-open a session and post resume_token to request server to replay from last stable checkpoint (server may accept or require canonical re-generation).
   - Resume semantics: server may (a) replay subsequent frames, (b) re-run tool-calls if not idempotent and client requested, or (c) fall back to sending a summarized recovery frame and continuing.

5) Failure and fallback models (priority order)
   - Transient network blip: client reconnects and uses last checkpoint to resume; SDK retries exponential backoff.
   - Mid-toolcall server abort: emit error frame with retryable=false if tool failed permanently; SDK surfaces fallback UI hook and optionally requests alternative tool variants.
   - Model hallucinated tool call (incorrectly requested): server can emit tool_call_abort with reason; SDK maps to user-visible warning.
   - Capacity fallback: server sends degraded_mode frame recommending a cheaper model variant or static cached result, with a reason code. SDKs surface cost/latency tradeoff prompt to developers.

6) Backpressure and interrupt semantics
   - Clients can send an in-channel control frame (over bidirectional WS or out-of-band POST for HTTP streams) to request: pause, resume, or cancel a specific call_id.
   - Pause: server buffers up to configured bytes; server may respond with pause_ack and begin emitting a "paused" state occasionally.
   - Cancel: server emits tool_call_abort and final error frame referencing call_id.
   - Recommendation: Default SDK exposes two primitives: stream.pause(reason?) and stream.cancel(). Lower-level API exposes onFrame hooks and backpressure signals.

7) SDK ergonomics (JS + Python sketch)
   - Primary abstraction: ResponseStream object with these events: on('init', data), on('frame', Frame), on('checkpoint', token), on('error', Error), on('complete').
   - For tool calls: responseStream.startToolProxy(callSpec) returns a ToolCall object with .on('progress'), .on('result'), .cancel(), .meta.
   - Provide typed Frame interfaces: PartialTextFrame {text, delta, offset?}, StructuredEventFrame {schema, data}, ToolCallFrame {call_id, tool, args}. For languages with typing, generate types from canonical schema in repo.
   - Default handlers: SDK should supply a minimal parser that maps frames to higher-level convenience callbacks: onTextAppend, onStructured(schemaName, parsedData), onToolRequest(callSpec) where callSpec exposes accept/decline/defaultResponse helpers.

8) Migration & compatibility
   - Existing streaming endpoints continue unchanged. New typed-frame endpoint is opt-in. Provide a compatibility header that asks server to wrap typed frames into plain-text markers for legacy clients.
   - Provide server-side adapter that can translate typed frames into delta-jsonp style partial_text only streams for customers who cannot upgrade SDKs quickly.

9) Observability and ops considerations
   - Each frame must include minimal tracing context (trace_id, span_id) and server timestamps.
   - Checkpoints should log size and frequency to telemetry; large number of resume attempts is a signal for model instability or client UX issues.
   - Tool-call metrics: latency, retry counts, abort rates, and mismatch rates (tool_call_start without result) surfaced per-customer.

10) Security & privacy notes
   - Resume tokens must never contain PII in plaintext; they are opaque server-signed blobs.
   - When tool_call frames reference external URLs or attach binary artifacts, ensure signed short-lived URLs or require customer-managed storage connectors.

Open questions (short list):
- Checkpoint frequency tradeoff: developer config vs. server heuristics.
- How to express schema evolution for structured_event frames without tight coupling? (versioning vs. extensible union types)
- Efficiency vs. correctness for re-running tool calls on resume (who bears cost?), and opt-in async semantics for heavy tool calls.
- Native mobile support where long-lived WS is unreliable — should we favor smaller checkpoint intervals for mobile?

Next steps & milestones (proposal):
- Week 1-2: internal design review with serving-runtime and SDK owners; finalize frame schema v0.1.
- Week 3-4: implement server handshake + checkpoint encoding prototype; add telemetry hooks.
- Week 5-8: JS SDK first-class support + integration test harness with simulated network flaps.
- Week 9-12: Python SDK parity + beta customers (select partner teams).

Notes to reviewers / asks:
- Piing infra/serving: is the checkpoint encoding feasible to generate cheaply on our runtime?
- Piing SDK leads: what minimal surface do you need to unblock client adoption in 4 weeks?
- Please review tool_call lifecycle; especially around retries and cost attribution when replays occur.

Rough cost/impact estimate (ballpark)
- Engineering: 2 backend engineers (runtime + orchestration) for 8 weeks, 2 SDK engineers (JS + Python) for 8 weeks, 0.5 PM/design.
- Risk: medium — primarily complexity in resume semantics and tool-call idempotency.

Appendix: example stream (conceptual chunk sequence)
- session_init {features: {checkpoints: true, max_checkpoint_ms: 15000}}
- partial_text {text: "Finding the best option"}
- partial_text {text: " for scheduling..."}
- structured_event {schema: "options_table_v1", data: [{time: "09:00", avail: true}, {time: "10:30", avail: false}]}
- tool_call_start {call_id: "c-123", tool: "calendar.lookup", args: {range: "today"}}
- checkpoint {token: "<opaque>"}
- tool_call_progress {call_id: "c-123", status: "running", percent: 40}
- tool_call_result {call_id: "c-123", result: {matches: 3}}
- partial_text {text: "I can book 09:00 or 11:00 — do you want me to?"}
- complete {}

End of document.
